title: Flipping an Image
spaceBreakdown:
- int temp, i, j, n: scalars → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input image (modified in place), returned reference
approach: For each row independently, reversing and inverting can be combined: the element at position j and the element at position n-1-j swap places AND both get bit-flipped (1-x). For odd n, the middle element (j == n-1-j) is just inverted in place. This is done in place with two pointers per row, so no extra matrix is allocated.
hints: For a single row, after you reverse it and then invert every bit, what happens to the pair of elements sitting at symmetric positions j and n-1-j? Each row is processed independently.
Use two pointers per row. For row [1,1,0] (n=3): swap ends while inverting - position 0 gets 1-0=1, position 2 gets 1-1=0, then invert the middle 1→0, yielding [1,0,0].

**Single cell (n = 1)** - only the middle element exists, odd length.
`Input: [[0]]` → `Expected: [[1]]`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the odd-middle inversion step → returns `[[0]]`

**Odd-length row, middle untouched** - the center index is never reached by the swap loop.
`Input: [[1,0,1]]` → `Expected: [[0,1,0]]`
⚠️ Bug: looping `j < n/2` and never inverting the middle → returns `[[0,0,0]]`

**All ones** - every cell identical, swap is a no-op so only inversion matters.
`Input: [[1,1],[1,1]]` → `Expected: [[0,0],[0,0]]`
⚠️ Bug: updating only `row[j]` and forgetting `row[n-1-j]` → returns `[[0,1],[0,1]]`

**Already symmetric row** - row equals its reverse, so swapping changes nothing.
`Input: [[1,0,0,1]]` → `Expected: [[0,1,1,0]]`
⚠️ Bug: swapping without inverting (`row[j]=row[n-1-j]`) → returns `[[1,0,0,1]]`

followUps.q: What if the image arrives as a stream of rows and you can only hold one row in memory?
followUps.a: Process each row on arrival with the same two-pointer swap-and-invert, then emit it. Time stays O(n^2), auxiliary space drops to O(n) for the single row buffer.

followUps.q: What if "flip" means vertical (reverse each column) instead of horizontal?
followUps.a: Apply the same swap-and-invert pairing but along columns: for each column c, swap and invert image[j][c] with image[n-1-j][c]. Time O(n^2), space O(1) in place.

followUps.q: What if each pixel is a 32-bit integer and "invert" means bitwise NOT?
followUps.a: Replace `1 - x` with `~x`; the swap-and-complement structure is identical. Time O(n^2), space O(1).
